topic: First-nonzero residual-hedge-rank frontier for minimum-cost causal experiment design. In finite simple bow-free semi-Markovian ADMGs with singleton target s and positive rational intervention costs, classify four-vertex hedges as complementary directed and bidirected spanning paths and prove r<=2 is hedge-free. For every ordered simple source graph H, use vertices x_u and one private guard z_e per edge e={u,v}, edges x_u->x_v->z_e->s, z_e<->x_u, and global s<->x_u spokes to prove the minimal residual-hedge clutter is exactly {{x_u,x_v,z_e}:e in E(H)}. Transfer unit-cost vertex cover to obtain NP/APX hardness at r=3 on bidirected trees of radius two. Prove a polynomial weighted factor-two LP rounding theorem, matching integrality-gap supremum two, and UGC-conditional (2-epsilon) hardness. Add promised-rank enumeration, scoped bounded-cardinality search, and an optimizer-or-rank-violation interface; do not claim unrestricted rank recognition or unconstrained weighted 3^k optimization. Consumer: Elahi et al.'s RC2/Gurobi workflow and Akbari et al.'s min_cost_intervention software. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: For every ordered H, every hedge contains a suffix x_v->z_e->s and bidirected connectivity forces its designated x_u; every intended triple is a four-vertex hedge. Guard replacement preserves vertex-cover optimum with unit costs. Edge counting classifies the first bow-free singleton hedge rank, parent/spouse rounding gives factor two, and complete-graph expansions match the LP gap. Exhaustive checks covered all 1,099 source graphs through five vertices and 1,900,363 residual subsets, plus K3,3 and the triangular prism; no unintended minimal hedge appeared. Rank-four and weighted-cardinality counterexamples removed two overclaims. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently or formally verify the universal reverse-inclusion theorem and rank-three parent/spouse rounding argument; the draft has complete informal proofs but is not Lean-checked. EARLY KILL TEST: Reimplement ancestry/connectivity enumeration independently through five source vertices and the named cubic cases; any hedge containing no intended triple kills the reduction. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_mcid_hedgerank_three_boundary.md.

open_problems.open_problem: For bow-free semi-Markovian ADMGs with a singleton target and minimal residual-hedge rank at most three, is minimum-cost causal-effect-identifying intervention design vertex-cover hard while admitting a tight factor-two approximation?

source_refs.claim: Appendix D.2 proves polynomial solvability for minimal hedge size at most two; fixed larger size permits polynomial enumeration but leaves an exponential hitting-set task.
source_refs.author: Sina Akbari, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Reformulates unrestricted MCID as WPMAX-SAT and ILP for exact practical solution, without establishing a bounded-hedge-rank approximation frontier.
source_refs.author: Sepehr Elahi, Sina Akbari, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash, Patrick Thiran

source_refs.claim: Assuming the Unique Games Conjecture, minimum vertex cover has no polynomial-time approximation within 2-epsilon.
source_refs.author: Subhash Khot, Oded Regev
source_refs.venue: Journal of Computer and System Sciences

open_problems.why_unsolved: The causal-design literature has a polynomial theorem at residual rank two and logarithmic hardness without a rank bound, but no retrieved source settles the first intervening rank. The missing step is not generic 3-Hitting Set: one must characterize which three-element residual-hedge sets can coexist under ADMG ancestry and bidirected-connectivity constraints, prove that a reduction introduces no unintended minimal hedges, and establish that this causal structure supports factor-two rather than generic factor-three rounding. The Khot-Regev threshold transfers only after an approximation-preserving realization of vertex-cover instances as rank-three causal clutters.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would give a rank-three residual-hedge representation theorem, an optimum-preserving reduction from weighted vertex cover, a polynomial weighted factor-two LP-rounding theorem, a family whose LP gaps approach two, and a UGC-conditional 2-epsilon lower bound.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from hedge obstruction to hitting-set optimization and tractable structural cases is the closest framing for a first-nonzero-rank frontier.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Latent confounding blocks observational identification -> proxy interventions remove hedge obstructions at heterogeneous costs -> residual hedge size controls the covering problem -> determine the exact complexity and approximation transition at rank three

method_exemplars.technique: Use hedge completeness and the ancestor-plus-c-component definition to prove both inclusion of every intended hedge and exclusion of unintended witnesses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired clutter theorem is correct only if its sets are exactly the graphical nonidentifiability witnesses for the target query.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer weighted vertex-cover half-integrality and threshold rounding after proving that the causal covering LP projects to a vertex-cover polytope.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed factor-two theorem and matching complete-graph gap depend on precisely this polyhedral structure.

method_exemplars.technique: Compose the UGC vertex-cover gap reduction with an optimum-preserving causal gadget and verify that auxiliary vertices do not distort approximation ratios.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the exact 2-epsilon barrier needed to match a factor-two causal-design approximation.

open_problems.open_problem: Under a promised bound r on minimal residual-hedge rank, can residual hedges be enumerated exactly once and MCID optimized by a certifying procedure that either returns its stated solution guarantee or exhibits a residual hedge larger than r?

source_refs.claim: For constant k, bounded-size subsets can be checked to enumerate minimal hedges, but the subsequent hitting-set task remains exponential.
source_refs.author: Sina Akbari, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Its SAT and ILP encodings avoid explicit unrestricted enumeration but neither certify a bounded-rank promise nor return a rank-violation witness.
source_refs.author: Sepehr Elahi, Sina Akbari, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash, Patrick Thiran

source_refs.claim: Develops parameterized search-tree algorithms for explicit weighted d-Hitting Set, whose edge-access assumption is absent for implicitly represented hedge clutters.
source_refs.author: Henning Fernau

source_refs.excerpt: Enum_G(O_G) emits exactly Theta_G(O_G), each numerical tuple once
give the finite input encoding and an operation/runtime bound for FrontierID

open_problems.why_unsolved: Bounded-rank hitting-set algorithms assume an explicit hyperedge list and may branch immediately on an uncovered edge, whereas MCID receives only an ADMG and query. Exact-once enumeration additionally requires a causal right-congruence: partial search traces can be merged only if their ancestry, district, root, and minimality states have identical future completions, and interventions can change all four. The rank-violation branch must be sound under the stated promise without implying unrestricted rank recognition, while weighted bounded-cardinality search must remain explicitly scoped rather than being advertised as an unconstrained 3^k optimizer.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would specify a promise-preserving |V|^{O(r)} enumeration and scoped search algorithm with canonical exact-once output, explicit delay and space bounds, and an interface returning either the optimum or stated approximation under the rank-r promise or a verifiable minimal residual hedge of size greater than r.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the practical bottleneck as replacing doubly exponential hedge search with solver-facing representations, naturally motivating a certifying bounded-rank interface.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Proxy interventions make blocked effects identifiable -> exhaustive minimal-hedge search is prohibitive -> SAT and ILP formulations make unrestricted instances practical -> promised low rank calls for a theorem-level optimizer-or-violation certificate

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt weighted d-Hitting-Set branching and its measure analysis after supplying a causal oracle for an uncovered minimal residual hedge.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest weighted bounded-cardinality search machinery and exposes exactly where implicit causal-clutter access replaces explicit set access.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the WPMAX-SAT or ILP encoding as a separation backend and augment it with constraints that force or refute a rank-r witness certificate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already translates the same MCID feasibility condition into mature solver primitives but lacks the promised-rank certificate.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt decomposable search with canonical representatives after proving a right-congruence for equivalent hedge-construction traces.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Distinct ancestry and district search traces can encode the same minimal hedge, so exact-once output requires quotienting search states.

open_problems.open_problem: Does rank-three MCID hardness persist for bow-free ADMGs with bounded mixed degree and planar underlying skeleton, or do these restrictions yield a polynomial-time algorithm?

source_refs.claim: Its MCID hardness reduction begins from weighted vertex cover, while its positive results concern tree-like directed or bidirected subgraphs and hedge size at most two.
source_refs.author: Sina Akbari, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Minimum vertex cover remains APX-complete on cubic graphs, providing a bounded-degree donor family for an approximation-preserving causal reduction.
source_refs.author: Paola Alimonti, Viggo Kann

source_refs.claim: Node cover remains NP-complete under planar and low-degree restrictions, but this does not provide a causal gadget preserving those restrictions.
source_refs.author: Michael R. Garey, David S. Johnson, Larry Stockmeyer

open_problems.why_unsolved: Bounded-degree or planar vertex-cover hardness does not transfer automatically: standard causal reductions use a common target and widespread bidirected spokes, creating a high-degree hub, destroying planarity, or generating extra hedges. The first proof step that must change is replacement of global target connectivity by local confounding connectors while retaining exact residual-hedge realization and optimum preservation. The retrieved literature contains no effect-identification hardness theorem imposing both restrictions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would be either an approximation-preserving bounded-degree planar ADMG construction proving NP or APX hardness at residual rank three, or a polynomial algorithm based on an explicit structural decomposition of that graph class.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates structural graph classes as routes to tractability and supplies the baseline vertex-cover reduction whose sparsity losses must be repaired.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: General MCID is NP-hard -> graph structure creates polynomial islands -> rank three is the first nontrivial covering regime -> bounded degree and planarity test whether hardness is intrinsic or caused by dense gadgets

method_exemplars.technique: Start from the L-reduction establishing cubic vertex-cover APX-hardness and attach locally degree-bounded causal edge gadgets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies an APX-hard source family with the degree control demanded by the destination theorem.

method_exemplars.technique: Use planar low-degree node-cover instances and a planar replacement gadget, proving through ancestry and connectivity that crossings and hub spokes are unnecessary.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the restricted source instances needed for planar hardness; the causal work is to preserve them through hedge realization.

open_problems.open_problem: How should one jointly choose rank-three proxy-intervention sets and allocate finite samples across their interventional distributions to minimize total acquisition cost subject to valid inference for a scalar causal effect?

source_refs.claim: Optimizes the fixed cost of proxy intervention sets required for identification but does not optimize finite-sample allocation or prove confidence guarantees.
source_refs.author: Sepehr Elahi, Sina Akbari, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash, Patrick Thiran

source_refs.claim: Derives influence-function estimators and efficiency bounds for identifiable effects in hidden-variable graphical models but does not select costly proxy experiments.
source_refs.author: Rohit Bhattacharya, Razieh Nabi, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: Optimizes adaptive treatment assignment for efficient ATE estimation but assumes direct ATE experimentation rather than hedge-hitting proxy laws.
source_refs.author: Masahiro Kato, Takuya Ishihara, Junya Honda, Yusuke Narita

open_problems.why_unsolved: MCID treats access to an interventional distribution as a fixed set cost and stops at identification, whereas influence-function work begins with a fixed identified statistical experiment. The first new proof step is a common influence-function representation across whichever observational and interventional laws the combinatorial design selects; selection and allocation then become coupled rather than separable. The retrieved literature treats proxy-law selection and efficiency-optimal sampling separately, not as one rank-constrained design problem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would derive efficient influence functions for the target under each feasible selected collection of proxy laws, formulate and solve or approximate the joint fixed-cost-plus-sampling allocation problem, and prove an asymptotically normal estimator with consistently estimated variance or an anytime-valid confidence sequence.

writing_exemplar.why: Its cost-aware proxy-experiment workflow supplies the application-facing motivation, with precision-aware design as the new endpoint.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Direct intervention may be infeasible -> cheaper proxy experiments can identify the effect -> feasible proxy collections have different fixed costs -> finite data make their information and sampling allocation part of the design objective

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt graphical fixing-based influence-function derivations and one-step estimators to the product model containing the selected observational and interventional laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly links hidden-variable graphical identification to semiparametric efficiency, the statistical rung absent from current MCID.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over efficiency-bound-minimizing allocation, adaptive AIPW martingale analysis, and anytime-valid confidence sequences.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result also chooses sampling frequencies to minimize causal-effect uncertainty, but over proxy laws constrained by hedge coverage.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the sound-and-complete reduction of general identification to classical identification subproblems to obtain the selected-law functional before differentiating it.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Joint proxy-law inference first requires a correct identifying functional from multiple interventional distributions under positivity.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the realizability and approximation frontier for singleton-target bow-free MCID when minimal residual hedges have rank four?

source_refs.claim: It isolates bounded hedge size, settles sizes one and two, and otherwise invokes generic bounded-size hitting set without characterizing causal-clutter realizability.
source_refs.author: Sina Akbari, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Proves NP-hardness of approximating k-uniform hypergraph vertex cover within k-1-epsilon for each fixed k at least three.
source_refs.author: Irit Dinur, Venkatesan Guruswami, Subhash Khot, Oded Regev

source_refs.claim: Under UGC, k-uniform hypergraph vertex cover is hard to approximate within k-epsilon, but arbitrary uniform clutters need not be causal-hedge realizable.
source_refs.author: Subhash Khot, Oded Regev
source_refs.venue: Journal of Computer and System Sciences

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic four-Hitting Set bounds do not automatically transfer because residual hedge families obey ancestry closure and bidirected connectivity, while shared gadget edges may create unintended smaller or additional minimal hedges. The retrieved causal papers do not characterize rank-four clutter realizability. The first step in adapting hypergraph-cover gap constructions is therefore to realize every source hyperedge as one and only one minimal residual hedge; failure may instead expose forbidden configurations that improve causal-specific approximability.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would be either a rank-four causal-clutter representation theorem transferring a sharp approximation lower bound and matching LP-rounding ratio, or a forbidden-configuration theorem yielding a strictly better approximation than general four-Hitting Set.

writing_exemplar.why: Its bounded-hedge-size section exposes the unsolved ladder beyond size two and is the natural motivation arc for the next rank.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: MCID is hedge hitting -> fixed hedge rank permits polynomial obstruction enumeration -> the first ranks have special graph structure -> rank four asks whether causal realizability inherits or beats general hypergraph hardness

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the multilayered-PCP gap instance for uniform hypergraph vertex cover through an approximation-preserving ADMG realization gadget.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the analogous rank-bounded cover gap whose transfer would determine the unconditional hardness side of a rank-four frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer the UGC hypergraph vertex-cover gap only after proving exact minimal-hedge realization and cost preservation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its k-epsilon threshold is the natural candidate barrier if rank-four hedge clutters are sufficiently universal.

literature_map:
1. Shpitser and Pearl (AAAI 2006) provide the complete hedge obstruction criterion for interventional identification.
2. Huang and Valtorta (UAI 2006) independently establish completeness of do-calculus, grounding hedge certificates semantically.
3. Bareinboim and Pearl (UAI 2012, arXiv:1210.4842) show how experiments on surrogate variables can identify otherwise blocked effects.
4. Lee, Correa, and Bareinboim (AAAI 2020, DOI 10.1609/aaai.v34i09.7119) characterize identification from mixed observational and interventional inputs using thickets and hedgelets.
5. Kivva et al. (UAI 2022, arXiv:2206.01081) repair gID under positivity and reduce it to classical identification subproblems.
6. Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (ICML 2022; JMLR 2025, arXiv:2205.02232) reduce MCID to minimum-weight hitting set and give exact and logarithmic algorithms.
7. Their bounded-hedge analysis proves polynomiality through size two but gives no rank-three complexity or approximation theorem.
8. Elahi et al. (NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2407.05330) encode unrestricted MCID as WPMAX-SAT and ILP; they do not provide a low-rank classification or promise certificate.
9. Kandasamy, Bhattacharyya, and Honavar (AAAI 2019, DOI 10.1609/aaai.v33i01.33012876) optimize interventions covering all effects, a different objective from single-query MCID.
10. Lindgren et al. (arXiv:1810.11867) and Addanki et al. (ICML 2020, arXiv:2005.11736) study cost-aware causal-structure learning rather than hedge-hitting effect identification.
11. Nemhauser and Trotter (1974, DOI 10.1007/BF01580222) supply the half-integral vertex-cover machinery behind tight factor-two rounding.
12. Singh (ORL 2019, DOI 10.1016/j.orl.2019.03.015) relates the vertex-cover LP gap to fractional chromatic number, with complete graphs approaching two.
13. Khot and Regev (JCSS 2008, DOI 10.1016/j.jcss.2007.06.019) give the UGC-conditional 2-epsilon vertex-cover barrier and its uniform-hypergraph extension.
14. Dinur, Guruswami, Khot, and Regev (SICOMP 2005, DOI 10.1137/S0097539704443057) give k-1-epsilon hardness for k-uniform hypergraph vertex cover, leaving causal realizability as the transfer obstacle.
15. Fernau (TCS 2010), Abu-Khzam (JCSS 2010), Bhattacharya-Nabi-Shpitser (JMLR 2022), and Kato et al. (arXiv:2002.05308) supply adjacent bounded-rank search and efficient-inference techniques not yet integrated into MCID.
